title: AltaClaro and Verbit Launch DepoSim, an AI-Powered Deposition Simulator for Litigators
author: Bob Ambrogi

dom.t: AI simulation: Practice substitutes remain unvalidated

st.t: AI simulation: Practice substitutes remain unvalidated
st.an: The source supports AI simulation as repeatable, realistic deposition practice with prompt, rubric-based feedback and optional partner coaching. Its evidence is limited to demonstrated functionality and company-reported participant satisfaction, not comparative skill gains or validated transfer to consequential client work, matching the synthesis’s cautious proposition.
qs: For each category, the feedback identifies what went well, what needed improvement, and how to improve, along with specific transcript references, citing the point in the transcript where a particular issue arose.
According to the companies, participants logged more than 160 hours of testing, and 97% strongly agreed that DepoSim is valuable for litigation training, while 94% said they would use it again.

kp.k: AI simulation targets gaps in associate deposition training
kp.d: Ambrogi reports the 2026 launch of DepoSim, developed by AltaClaro and Verbit to offer litigators unlimited, on-demand deposition practice with structured feedback. AltaClaro argues that conventional actor-based and off-site training is expensive, infrequent and difficult to scale, leaving junior associates with limited practice before questioning real witnesses. This is the company's rationale for the product, rather than a demonstrated finding about training outcomes.
qs: The product is designed to give litigators unlimited, on-demand opportunities to practice conducting depositions in realistic scenarios, then receive structured, objective feedback on how well they performed.
A junior associate may handle very few practice depositions before being put in front of a real witness, where the stakes are high and the client’s patience is limited.
“It fills a crucial gap that traditional, costly, and infrequent deposition training models simply cannot address.”

kp.k: Repeated practice underpins the proposed model of lawyer development
kp.d: AltaClaro frames DepoSim through Deliberate Practice, borrowing from sports and performing arts a model of repeated, feedback-intensive skill development rather than passive observation or isolated exposure. The proposed mechanism is repeated depositions with adjustable variables until core advocacy skills become internalized.
qs: AltaClaro frames DepoSim within its broader philosophy of Deliberate Practice – the principle, borrowed from sports and performing arts, that skills are built through repeated, feedback-intensive repetition rather than passive observation or one-time exposure.
The idea is that a lawyer should be able to run a deposition as many times as needed, adjusting variables each time, until the fundamental skills are internalized.

kp.k: Configurable AI participants enable live spoken deposition practice
kp.d: The reported demonstration used a fictional franchise dispute and showed a lawyer questioning an AI witness while simulated opposing counsel raised objections. Users can upload outlines, reference exhibits and select among five witness personalities and five opposing-counsel styles. Speech technologies and large language models generate dynamic responses, enabling practice with varied interpersonal challenges rather than only a fixed script.
qs: DepoSim uses text-to-speech, speech-to-text, and large language model capabilities to voice the witness, opposing counsel and court reporter in real time.
The user speaks their questions aloud; the witness and opposing counsel respond dynamically.
At one point, opposing counsel objected to a compound question and to an argumentative question, much as one might expect a real attorney to do.

The interface also displays the uploaded deposition outline and any pre-marked exhibits on screen during the session, so the attorney can reference their materials while questioning the witness, mirroring real-world practice.

kp.k: Rubric-based evaluation connects coaching to specific transcript passages
kp.d: In the demonstration, feedback arrived within minutes and evaluated skills including introductions, oath administration, exhibit handling, questioning, follow-up, witness management, time management and articulacy. Reports identify strengths, weaknesses and improvements with transcript references and category scores. AltaClaro says evaluation extends beyond outline adherence to responsiveness to witnesses; downloadable reports are intended to support additional coaching by supervising partners.
qs: When the simulation ends, DepoSim generates a structured evaluation tied to a standardized training rubric.

For each category, the feedback identifies what went well, what needed improvement, and how to improve, along with specific transcript references, citing the point in the transcript where a particular issue arose.
Both the full transcript and the feedback report are downloadable as PDFs, which AltaClaro envisions attorneys sharing with supervising partners for additional coaching conversations.

It also evaluates responsiveness to the witness, picking up on things the witness said and following up appropriately, which reflects a more sophisticated view of deposition competency than simple script adherence.

kp.k: Beta feedback reports strong acceptance, not measured skill gains
kp.d: The five-week beta cohort included six Am Law 100 firms: Orrick, Herrington & Sutcliffe; K&L Gates; McDermott Will & Emery; Littler Mendelson; Taft Stettinius & Hollister; and Brownstein Hyatt Farber Schreck. According to the companies, participants logged more than 160 hours of testing, 97% strongly agreed the tool was valuable for litigation training, and 94% would use it again. These reported measures concern user perceptions and intended reuse; the document supplies no participant count or measured improvement in advocacy performance.
qs: The launch follows testing with a notable early-adopter cohort that participated in a five-week beta pilot.
According to the companies, participants logged more than 160 hours of testing, and 97% strongly agreed that DepoSim is valuable for litigation training, while 94% said they would use it again.

kp.k: Customer testimonials emphasize realism and practice without client expense
kp.d: Customer remarks carried in press materials describe the simulation as realistic and its feedback as unusually useful. A participating partner compared the feedback favorably with feedback from attorneys, while a senior associate valued practicing departures from an outline without using a real person or spending client money. These are reported testimonials, not independently established comparisons of training quality or cost.
qs: User feedback cited in the press materials included a participating partner describing the experience as “frighteningly realistic” and saying the feedback was “better than I’ve received from attorneys.”
A senior associate noted the value of “practicing going off-book with not a real human while not wasting your client’s money.”

kp.k: Partnership combines legal pedagogy with transcription and AI capabilities
kp.d: The companies began collaborating at Legalweek 2025 and formally launched the beta in fall 2025. AltaClaro supplied pedagogy, learner experience and deposition scenarios; Verbit supplied the underlying transcription and AI technology. The account describes a division of product-development responsibilities between a legal training company and a transcription technology company.
qs: The two companies began their collaboration at Legalweek 2025 and formally launched a beta in fall 2025.

The division of labor follows each company’s core competency: AltaClaro designed the pedagogy, the learner experience and the realistic deposition scenarios; Verbit built the underlying technology, including high-speed secure transcription and the AI agent capabilities that power the simulated witness and counsel.

kp.k: Planned expansion extends simulation beyond depositions
kp.d: At launch, DepoSim was available to existing AltaClaro clients and new firms. The companies say pilot feedback is informing expansion into additional litigation subjects and activities, including trial practice, oral arguments, client interviews and negotiation; these are roadmap claims. The demonstration already showed multiple witness types within one matter. AltaClaro presents DepoSim as the spoken-advocacy counterpart to Benchmark360, its AI feedback product for written legal work.
qs: Based on pilot feedback, the companies say they are expanding the platform’s scenario library to cover commercial litigation, employment law, intellectual property, expert witness depositions, trial practice, oral arguments, client interviews and negotiation.

The demo showed that case files can include multiple witnesses – a plaintiff’s witness, a third-party witness, and an expert witness – allowing attorneys to practice a full range of deposition scenarios within a single matter.
This launch follows AltaClaro’s Benchmark360 product, which applies AI to provide feedback on written legal work product.

cl.s: Concrete claim or prediction about how AI changes legal services, the legal profession, or legal markets (or, for a cross-domain source, its own domain)

pts.k: AI simulation is presented as making repeated, realistic deposition training available on demand, addressing the cost, logistics and limited frequency of traditional associate training.
pts.d: Bob Ambrogi reports that DepoSim provides spoken practice with an AI witness, opposing counsel and court reporter, with configurable personalities and dynamic responses. AltaClaro attributes the training gap to traditional exercises being costly, infrequent and difficult to scale. Its CEO, Abdi Shayesteh, claims repeated simulation can turn legal knowledge into practiced advocacy competence. These are claims about augmenting lawyer development, not replacing lawyers in actual depositions.

pts.k: AI-generated, transcript-linked evaluations are presented as supporting targeted improvement in oral advocacy rather than merely checking compliance with a prepared outline.
pts.d: Ambrogi describes category-level scores and feedback identifying strengths, weaknesses and improvement steps, with transcript references. AltaClaro says the rubric assesses responsiveness and appropriate follow-up as well as prepared questioning. Downloadable reports are intended to support further coaching by supervising partners. Verbit CEO Yair Amsterdam frames the product as an example of AI elevating legal performance; that broader performance claim is distinct from the demonstrated ability to generate feedback.

cl.s: Evidence basis offered for the claim (data, benchmarks, cases, experience, authority, or none)

pts.k: The evidence offered consists of company-reported pilot participation and satisfaction, a product demonstration, and selected practitioner testimonials.
pts.d: The five-week beta included six Am Law 100 firms: Orrick, K&L Gates, McDermott Will & Emery, Littler Mendelson, Taft Stettinius & Hollister, and Brownstein Hyatt Farber Schreck. The companies report more than 160 testing hours, 97% strongly agreeing the product is valuable for litigation training, and 94% saying they would use it again. The article does not give the respondent count or report measured changes in real-world deposition performance. Ambrogi's demonstration account supplies examples of responsive simulated objections and transcript-specific feedback. Press-material testimonials supply subjective assessments of realism and usefulness, not comparative performance measurements.

cl.s: Stated or implied timeframe, conditions or qualifications under which the claim holds

pts.k: Deposition simulation is described as available at the 2026 launch, following a fall 2025 beta; expansion into additional subjects and advocacy tasks is a roadmap claim without a completion date.
pts.d: The companies began collaborating at Legalweek 2025 and formally launched the beta in fall 2025. At publication, DepoSim is available to existing AltaClaro clients and new firms. The demonstrated feedback arrived within minutes. The training benefit is framed through deliberate practice: repeated sessions, feedback and adjustment rather than a single exposure. The companies say they are expanding the scenario library into further litigation areas and activities, but the article supplies no rollout deadline.

cl.s: Who is affected and how (market segment, role, firm type, clients, or the public)

pts.k: The immediate beneficiaries identified are litigators, especially junior associates, law-firm training teams and supervising partners; clients are described as indirectly benefiting from practice outside live matters.
pts.d: The article focuses on associate development at large firms, with early adoption among Am Law 100 firms, although availability extends to new firms generally. Associates can rehearse questioning, handling objections and departing from an outline without using a real witness or a client's matter as the training setting. Supervising partners can use transcripts and reports for coaching. An unnamed senior associate's testimonial frames this as avoiding expenditure of client money during practice; the article provides no quantified client savings. The planned expansion would extend the training use case to other litigation specialties and activities such as interviewing and negotiation.
